title: Sampling graphs with given degrees
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's proof (2026) that the switch chain on simple graphs with a prescribed degree vector mixes in polynomial time for every graphical degree vector, with mixing time at most 2n^8, which settles the simple-graph case of the Kannan-Tetali-Vempala conjecture, and an exact uniform sampler with expected polynomial running time. The first lesson defines the chain, proves that switches connect all graphs with the same degrees, and reduces the theorem to the operator inequality H^2 >= H for the sum H of the pair resampling projections. The second proves a variance inequality for random binary matrices with three rows and applies it to vertex triples. The third controls the interaction of disjoint pairs by an inequality on slices of the Boolean cube and proves H^2 >= H. The fourth removes the remaining bias of the chain by a rare exact branch.
